analysis:
All three changed files are tests under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/.../ClusterApproval/. No production code is in this batch, so no direct security regression is observable here. The tests describe production behavior that is not supplied and was not reviewed.

1. ClusterApprovalServiceStartTests.swift (lines 48-54, 116-139): tests that a supervised service's member part beats into its own heartbeat file (ClusterServiceAgent.partHealthPath) and never into the supervisor's file. They also check that an empty heartbeat env value is passed through empty. This is availability and liveness behavior (the supervisor restarting a healthy service); no secrets or authorization are involved. The production partEnvironment code is not visible here.

2. ClusterApprovalTensorAssistantTests.swift (new, lines 1-74): tests that a Qwen tensor-parallel setup with a tensorAssistant is refused by the leader's own check before any part stops or anything is sent to the peer. The peer also refuses it on its own. A pair without the assistant is saved on both Macs. The refusal fails closed, and the peer-side check means an older-build leader cannot push an unqualified assistant setup. This matches the intent of TB-011 and T-054: unqualified features are not offered to the coordinator. The production enforcement is outside the supplied evidence.

3. ClusterApprovalWatchTests.swift (lines 30-35, 162, 177-304): tests a one-hour (ClusterApprovalFallback.failingSeconds) expiry of the 'failing' set-aside, with a setAt timestamp. A legacy record without setAt is treated as past the hour, and a future setAt (clock set back) is released. Quick ends the coordinator caused (negotiationFailed) no longer count toward the failing limit, while local-cause ends still do. Open question for integration: the retry window re-offers a failing approval hourly and could weaken the 'not taken again' safeguard. The approval still passes each Mac's own check and the coordinator remains authoritative (A-016, T-053), and the tests show a refused or ended approval is not re-offered. Excluding coordinator-side ends from the count is availability behavior only. None of this is evidenced as a regression in this test-only batch.

The production changes (ClusterApprovalCheck, ApprovalSetAside.setAt, ClusterService.partEnvironment, memberQuickEnds) need review if they are in another batch.
